page: Amazon Web Services m5n.2xlarge is a general-purpose, network- and EBS-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance provides 8 vCPUs across 4 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading enabled (2 threads per core). It is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled, meaning all storage relies on network-attached Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes. There are no GPUs present on this instance.

Benchmark data shows a mix of average and weak performance profiles. The instance achieves average results in multi-core CPU performance, passmark CPU scores, and memory bandwidth tests, including read-only small block (376.11 GB/sec) and large block (49.53 GB/sec) operations. However, single-core performance is weak, as evidenced by the stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Cryptographic and extended instruction tests, such as the PassMark CPU encryption test, perform in the average range, aided by hardware flags like AES and AVX-512. LLM inference speeds are average for small models (135M) but drop to poor (bottom 10%) for medium models (7B).

Given its hardware profile, the m5n.2xlarge offers a balanced resource density of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for workloads requiring steady network throughput and moderate compute resources without the overhead of local NVMe storage. With a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps, it is suitable for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, database operations, and software compilation. It is less suitable for heavy single-threaded processing, complex physics simulations, or large-scale machine learning inference.
